Hello readers!  
I’m excited to share my journey of interviewing at Flipkart, which led to an offer for a **6-month internship (January to July)** and a full-time **Software Development Engineer (SDE-1) role**. I got this opportunity through **Flipkart’s Girls Wanna Code 5.0 program**, a mentorship initiative designed to support Women in Tech.

## Round 1: The Technical Test (HackerRank)

Duration: 1 Hour 30 Minutes

The first hurdle was an intense online assessment. It was divided into 4 mandatory sections, and the tricky part was that you cannot switch between sections — each is time-bounded.

* **CS MCQs (30 mins):** 15 questions covering OS, DBMS, and Networks. (+5 for correct, -2 for incorrect).
* **Programming (40 mins):** 2 Medium-level coding questions.
* **Subjective Section (15 mins):** 2 behavioral/situational questions.

Round 2 (Technical + HR)
Again discussed a project from my resume.
HR: Challenges faced while doing the project.

DSA Question: Given two strings s and p, find all starting indices of anagrams of p in s.
JavaScript questions were linked to the DSA problem — for example, how I would implement the logic and handle the results on the frontend for this DSA question.
Follow-ups, discussed edge cases, and time complexity.

Round 3 (Technical)

DSA Question: Given currency conversion rates, determine if there exists a conversion path that can yield a profit.

## **Technical Round 2:**

As every round was eliminatory, I gained some confidence and sat there waiting for my turn. By the time the interview started, it was already 8:30pm, and some students weren’t even done with their first round. As the interview began with an introduction, I really wanted them to ask me about my projects or internship, but my interviewer went straight into DSA. He gave me a question on Anagrams, and I was able to code it pretty easily, explaining each step. Then, he gave me another question on strings, which I don’t remember specifically now, but after giving it some thought, I was able to code it and explain the edge cases as well. We then had a discussion on OOPS concepts and what are header files in C++. After the interview ended, I had a good feeling as the interviewer hinted that I would be called for the third interview as well. For GS, it is said that if you get to sit in the 3rd round, that means you have high chances of getting selected.
